subject: MAP: cost-model interlock + canary plan
messages:
From: Kerry Nolan <kerry@medicalogic.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@medicalogic.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions and gating items

Rafael,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. We want to lock the MAP milestones this week so procurement can start redlines next Monday. Two asks up front so our CFO can sign off on the pilot economics:

1) A concise tokens-per-dollar model for the two flows we discussed (NLP-call summary + retrieval prompt), with 90/95th percentile latency targets and per-request batching assumptions.
2) A short canary plan for the pilot: how you’ll degrade (quantized model / cached responses) if we hit the latency or spend thresholds.

We attached the workbook outline from our side — if you can drop a completed sheet by EOD Friday, procurement will have enough to start T&Cs.

Kerry
Director, Platform Integrations
MedicaLogic

[Attachment: medlogical_map_template.xlsx]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Kerry Nolan <kerry@medicalogic.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions and gating items

Kerry — thanks, this is helpful. Quick read-through and some clarifying Qs so we align the model before filling the workbook: 

- Can you confirm expected volume profile (spikes vs steady): you mentioned 15 reqs/sec peak during business hours on the product demo; is that sustained for a 2-hr window or short bursts?
- For the retrieval step, do you plan to use full-document embeddings per query or a filter-then-embed approach? That changes embedding units and cache hit rates a lot.

High-level plan from our side: Grace will own tokens/$ sensitivity sheet (3 scenarios: baseline, 2x, 5x). Karthik will validate batching and latency tradeoffs and propose a canary fallback order: 1) prefix caching, 2) 8-bit quantized variant, 3) route to cheaper region for background jobs.

We can do an internal pass and send the populated workbook + one-pager with gating thresholds by Thu 4/15. If that works, procurement can start redlines on Mon 4/19.

-Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: rdm-map-notes.txt]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Kerry Nolan <kerry@medicalogic.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions and gating items

On Sun, Apr 11, 2027 at 11:05 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Kerry — thanks, this is helpful. Quick read-through and some clarifying Qs so we align the model before filling the workbook: 
> 
> - Can you confirm expected volume profile (spikes vs steady): you mentioned 15 reqs/sec peak during business hours on the product demo; is that sustained for a 2-hr window or short bursts?
> - For the retrieval step, do you plan to use full-document embeddings per query or a filter-then-embed approach? That changes embedding units and cache hit rates a lot.

Kerry — answering Rafael’s bullets: we expect 1.5k unique active users/day, with a daily peak ~15 reqs/sec for two 1-hour windows (AM/PM). For retrieval, our app will filter by patient ID first, then run a small set (<=5) of embeddings against a short-list; so cache hit rate should be moderate.

Karthik and Rafael — quick notes from my side:
- Baseline tokens per request (combined prompt + response) we observed on similar pilots: 900 tokens median, 2.1k tokens 95p.
- With batching turned on (agg window 30ms, max batch 8) we reduce GPU tokens/sec by ~18% in practice and can preserve p95 latency under 600ms for the smaller model.
- Cache assumptions: filter-then-embed yields ~35% cache hit on the embedding shortlist in our ops benchmarks; prefix caching for common system prompts gives another ~12% effective token reduction.

I’ll take the tokens/$ sensitivity table and populate the three scenarios. Karthik — can you run a brief micro-benchmark for the 8-bit variant and share latency quantiles by EOD Wed? Rafael — do you want me to include a proposed spend SLO where we automatically throttle non-critical calls at 80% of budget?

Grace
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: batching_latency_samples.csv]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Kerry Nolan <kerry@medicalogic.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions and gating items

Thanks team — short update and an action list.

- I kicked off a quick canary bench with the 8-bit builds (small variant) and measured p50/p95 token latency with batch sizes 1/4/8. Early results (local env): p95 <= 580ms with batch=4, p95 <= 720ms with batch=8 for 2.1k-token inputs. I’ll reproduce on dedicated infra tomorrow and add CPU/GPU utilization numbers.
- Proposed canary escalation order (explicit):
  1) Enable prefix caching and embedding shortlist cache (expected spend reduction 22–28%).
  2) Switch reads to 8-bit quantized model for non-sensitive endpoints (cost ~30% lower, moderate quality diffs).
  3) For sustained overload, re-route background batch jobs to our lower-cost region; keep SLOs for syncronous UX intact.

Action items:
- Grace: populate tokens/$ sensitivity sheet (due Thu 4/15).
- Rafael: confirm budget SLO and whether procurement needs the spend threshold in plain dollars or % of contract.
- Lauren: can you attach the standard MAP gating clause (SLA/credits) to the Drive doc?

I’ll upload the bench CSVs and a short readme to the linked Drive.

—Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
